---
title: "R and R Markdown: restart the familiar workflow"
---

Allow 30–60 minutes if you need a refresher. The goal is to reopen a project,
read a table, calculate one result and Knit a report. You do not need to learn
a new programming language or molecular modelling system for this course.

## 1. Open an ordinary project folder

Download the [student ZIP](../downloads/organic-chemistry-student.zip), locate
it in your file manager and extract it. Open the extracted
`organic-chemistry.Rproj` in RStudio. Work inside the extracted folder rather
than opening files inside the ZIP.

The project root contains `report.Rmd`, the project file and `data/`.
The report refers to `data/amounts.csv`: that is a relative path starting from
the report's folder. Keep the report there. Save derived files in `output/`
and leave the original CSVs unchanged.

## 2. Check the software once

Use the R/RStudio environment supported by your programme. The course uses
`readr`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `knitr` and `rmarkdown`, the same report workflow
as the introductory computing materials. If these packages are absent from
your own installation, install them once from the R console:

```r
install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
```

Installation needs network access. In a managed teaching environment follow
the provided setup instructions instead of changing its installation. RStudio
normally supplies the Pandoc program used when knitting HTML reports.

## 3. Read and inspect before calculating

Run the following in an R script or a code chunk, not the terminal:

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
amounts <- read_csv("data/amounts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
amounts
names(amounts)
```

Expect two reactant rows. Check the units in the column names and the
[data dictionary](../reference/data.qmd). A row is a reagent in a constructed
reaction example, not an independent experiment.

## 4. Check one calculation by hand

Amount in mol = mass in g / molar mass in g/mol. For salicylic acid,
1.3812 g / 138.12 g/mol = 0.0100 mol = 10.0 mmol.

```r
amounts <- amounts |>
  mutate(amount_mol = mass_g / molar_mass_g_mol,
         amount_mmol = 1000 * amount_mol)
amounts
```

Explain why the result changes by a factor of 1000 when changing mol to mmol.
A variable name is a reminder of units; R does not automatically enforce them.

## 5. Knit from a fresh session

Open `report.Rmd`. Replace the author name, save, then click **Knit** to create
the HTML report. The starter already creates every object it uses. Restart R
and Knit again to check that saved code and data are sufficient.

In an Rmd, prose belongs outside code chunks. R belongs between the chunk's
opening and closing triple backticks. Use the editor's Insert Chunk command
if you lose track of those boundaries. The teaching website uses `.qmd` files;
your student report remains `.Rmd`.

## Recover from common errors

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| “Cannot open file” | Is the ZIP extracted? Is `report.Rmd` beside the `data/` folder? Is the filename exact, including its extension? |
| “Object not found” | Is the object created in an earlier chunk in the report? Running a command in the console does not add it to the report |
| “Could not find function” | Load the package in the report's setup chunk; check spelling |
| A column contains text instead of numbers | Inspect the CSV, decimal marks and import messages; do not silently coerce errors away |
| The output did not change | Save the Rmd and Knit again; confirm you opened the new HTML file |
| A calculation is 1000 times too large | Check g/mg and mol/mmol conversions |

Ask for setup help if you cannot open the project or Knit the supplied starter.
Keep working on the paper chemistry questions while the software issue is resolved.
